newsitem.title: UK: Lead and zinc offtake seen higher in 1997 - ILZSG.
newsitem.headline: Lead and zinc offtake seen higher in 1997 - ILZSG.

text.p: Consumption of both lead and zinc is expected to rise this year, from 1996, the International Lead and Zinc Study Group (ILZSG) said.

Global lead consumption is seen rising 1.9 percent to 5.94 million tonnes, while world zinc offtake is forecast rising 3.5 percent to 7.72 million tonnes, the ILZSG said in a release following its spring meeting.
It also said that refined lead production will rise, but zinc availability will fall.
Global refined lead production is expected to rise 3.4 percent to 5.77 million tonnes, which largely reflects a nine percent recovery in European output.
ILZSG said that because there will probably be a reduction in imports of lead from Eastern countries, Western world suply and demand is likely to be closely balanced.
In zinc, world mine production is forecast falling 2.6 percent to 7.02 million tonnes, although this includes preliminary Chinese data which is subject to revision.
However, refined zinc output will be higher at 7.60 million tonnes, up 3.6 percent.
"New capacity in China will reinforce its position as the world's largest producer of zinc metal with an increase of 71,000 tonnes to 1.5 million tonnes," the ILZSG said.
Net imports from the East, particlarly China are likely to be above 1996 levels.
"However, Western World demand is forecast to continue well in excess of available supply with a further drawdown in reported stocks," it said.
